column1: # Documentation sources indexed into the local docs MCP server.
# Format (tab-separated):  <library>
# The third column holds real CLI flags, NOT JSON. This is deliberate: the MCP `scrape_docs` tool
# accepts only url/library/version/maxPages/maxDepth/scope/followRedirects/preserveHashes and
# SILENTLY DROPS anything else — exclude/include patterns are CLI-only. Routing through the CLI and
# keeping the flags verbatim means what you write here is what the crawler gets.
# --max-pages is a hard cap spent in link order, so exclude the big low-value trees or they starve
# the pages you actually want. Three offenders, all three seen here:
#   1. changelogs / release-notes   (one huge page that mentions every feature once)
#   2. translated doc trees         (FastAPI ships ~20 languages inside the default subpages scope)
#   3. mirrored version trees       (helm.sh/docs == helm.sh/docs/v3 — half the budget bought
#                                    nothing AND every search returned each page twice)
# Use glob patterns (**/x/**). Regex form (/pattern/) also exists but globs are what is verified here.
# Two traps that produce a 1-page "success" instead of an error:
#   - A cross-host redirect. The default `subpages` boundary is computed from the URL you gave, so
#     after a redirect to another host nothing matches. pydantic does this: docs.pydantic.dev/latest/
#     301s to pydantic.dev/docs/validation/... — point at the real target and scope by hostname.
#   - A client-rendered site. In the default `fetch` mode the crawler sees no links at all in
#     playwright.dev's HTML; it needs --scrape-mode playwright.
# Always sanity-check the page count: a big doc site returning single digits means one of these.
